item.title: Blue drum case
item.description: Saurabh Rajput returned home from sea duty to celebrate his wife's and daughter's birthdays. While home, his wife Muskan and her lover Sahil conspired to eliminate him. On March 3, after eating sedated food, Saurabh was killed and dismembered in his home. To obscure the timeline, the accused purchased a 250 kg capacity blue plastic drum and sacks of cement from local markets, sealed Saurabh's remains inside, and fled on a vacation trip to Himachal Pradesh using Saurabh's phone to post updates and deceive family members. Following growing suspicion and police questioning upon their return, Muskan eventually confessed to her parents and police, leading to the recovery of the drum.

item.title: The Satyam Computer Services scandal
item.description: Often referred to as “India’s Enron,” the 2009 Satyam Computer Services scandal stands as one of the most notorious corporate frauds in Indian history. The deception unraveled on January 7, 2009, when the company’s founder and chairman, Byrraju Ramalinga Raju, confessed to systematically manipulating financial records for years, inflating revenues, profits, and cash balances to make the Hyderabad-based IT giant appear robust. To sustain the illusion, management forged bank statements, created fake invoices, and even invented roughly 10,000 "ghost" employees to siphoning off salary funds into real estate investments. The fraud, estimated at over ₹7,000 crore, finally collapsed after investors revolted against a desperate, conflicted bid to acquire two Raju-linked companies Maytas Infrastructure and Maytas Properties to plug the financial deficit. Following extensive investigations by the CBI, SEBI, and SFIO, a special court on April 9, 2015, convicted Raju and nine others, sentencing them to seven years of rigorous imprisonment for criminal conspiracy and falsification of accounts. To preserve business continuity and protect over 40,000 jobs, the Indian government swiftly dissolved the compromised board and facilitated the acquisition of Satyam by Tech Mahindra, while simultaneously enacting historic regulatory overhauls through the Companies Act of 2013 to enforce mandatory auditor rotation, strengthen independent director oversight, and tighten corporate governance frameworks nationwide.

item.title: Tandoor murder case
item.description: The Tandoor Murder Case (1995) involved Naina Sahni, who was murdered by her husband Sushil Sharma due to suspicion of an affair. Sharma shot her and, with the help of Keshav Kumar, tried to destroy the evidence by burning her body in a tandoor. Forensic investigation, DNA profiling, ballistic examination, and a second autopsy proved that Naina had died from gunshot injuries before being burned. The case highlighted the importance of forensic science in criminal investigations and became one of India's most famous murder cases.

item.title: The Sheena Bora Murder Case
item.description: The Sheena Bora murder case is a high-profile legal battle centered around identity deception, domestic conflict, and financial motives. To protect her status in elite society after marrying media tycoon Peter Mukerjea, Indrani Mukerjea hid that Sheena was her biological daughter, publicly presenting her as a younger sister. When Sheena became romantically involved with Peter's son, Rahul Mukerjea, Indrani vehemently opposed the relationship, driven by fears of social exposure and inheritance disputes. According to the CBI, on April 24, 2012, Indrani, her ex-husband Sanjeev Khanna, and driver Shyamvar Rai allegedly lured, sedated, and strangled Sheena in a rented car, later burning her remains in the Raigad district. Indrani covered up the crime for three years by sending fake emails and texts claiming Sheena had moved to the United States. The plot unraveled in August 2015 when the driver was arrested on an unrelated charge and confessed, leading to the arrests of all key suspects. Today, the trial is in its final stages in a special Mumbai court under a strict timeline to conclude, with all primary accused individuals currently out on bail
